newsitem.title: USA: Barney's summary judgment over leases denied.
newsitem.headline: Barney's summary judgment over leases denied.

text.p: U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge James Garrity denied Barney's Inc's motion for summary judgment about real estate agreements between Isetan of America and the U.S. retailer, Isetan and Barney's said.
The companies are disputing whether Isetan is the landlord of the properties where Barney's has its stores in mid-town Manhattan, Beverly Hills and Chicago.
Isetan claims that it is the landlord of the properties, while Barney's contends that the real estate agreement is not a lease but an equity arrangement.
The Bankruptcy Court will make its decision about the real estate agreements after a trial, the companies said in separate statements.
Isetan said in a statement that it is "gratified" by the judge's ruling and that it will show the court in a trial that Barney's owes Isetan rent for their use.
Barney's said it is confident that the court will find that the agreements are not leases.
The final verdict about the real estate could have a bearing upon where Japan's Isetan stands in Barney's Inc's bankruptcy.

If Isetan is a landlord, it would be able to make claims as a creditor against Barney's for rent owed to it. If the court finds that it is not a landlord, the properties could be considered a part of Barney's equity, placing Isetan at a disadvantage in the Chapter 11 reorganization.
Creditors and vendors get first claim to the assets of a bankrupt company over equity holders.
